In Daniel and Ezra it appears most often in its Haphel (causative) form, where kings and officials 'make known' dreams, decrees, and legal matters. The Peal (basic) stem covers ordinary knowing and perceiving, while the passive participle marks what is publicly recognized or established. Spanish and French translations consistently distinguish 'hacer saber / faire savoir' (cause to know) from 'conocer / connaître' (to know), confirming the causative-versus-basic split across the senses."
